rule-snelheid-bebouwd.question: What is the general maximum speed limit within built-up areas in Flanders, unless indicated otherwise?
options: 50 km/h
30 km/h
70 km/h
90 km/h
rule-snelheid-bebouwd.explanation: In Flanders and Wallonia, the standard speed limit in built-up areas is 50 km/h (art. 11.1). In the Brussels-Capital Region, the default is 30 km/h.

rule-snelheid-buiten-vl.question: What is the standard maximum speed limit outside built-up areas on Flemish roads since the speed reform, unless indicated otherwise?
options: 50 km/h
70 km/h
90 km/h
120 km/h
rule-snelheid-buiten-vl.explanation: In Flanders and Brussels, the standard speed limit outside built-up areas is 70 km/h (art. 11.2). Only in Wallonia does 90 km/h remain the default.

rule-snelheid-autosnelweg.question: What is the maximum speed limit on motorways in Belgium?
options: 100 km/h
110 km/h
120 km/h
130 km/h
rule-snelheid-autosnelweg.explanation: Under article 11.2.1°a, the maximum speed on Belgian motorways is 120 km/h, unless a traffic sign imposes a different limit.

rule-snelheid-min-autosnelweg.question: What minimum speed applies in principle on a motorway, provided traffic conditions allow?
options: 50 km/h
60 km/h
70 km/h
80 km/h
rule-snelheid-min-autosnelweg.explanation: Under article 11.2.2°, no driver on a motorway may drive at a speed below 70 km/h under normal conditions.

rule-alcohol-algemeen.question: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for a regular driver in Belgium?
options: 0.2 promille (0.09 mg/l UAL)
0.5 promille (0.22 mg/l UAL)
0.8 promille (0.35 mg/l UAL)
0.0 promille (zero tolerance)
rule-alcohol-algemeen.explanation: The general limit is 0.5 promille (grams per litre of blood), which corresponds to 0.22 mg per litre of exhaled alveolar air (art. 34 §1).

rule-alcohol-beroep.question: What stricter alcohol limit applies in Belgium to professional drivers (lorry, bus, taxi)?
options: 0.0 promille (zero tolerance)
0.2 promille (0.09 mg/l UAL)
0.5 promille (0.22 mg/l UAL)
0.8 promille (0.35 mg/l UAL)
rule-alcohol-beroep.explanation: For professional drivers, a strict limit of 0.2 promille (0.09 mg/l UAL) applies.

rule-gordel-algemeen.question: Must you wear a seat belt in the back seat of a passenger car?
options: No, it is only mandatory in the front seats.
Yes, wearing a seat belt is mandatory for every occupant in any equipped seat.
Only outside built-up areas.
Only on motorways.
rule-gordel-algemeen.explanation: Article 35.1 obliges all occupants of motor vehicles to wear a seat belt where one is provided.

rule-kinderzitje.question: Up to what body height must a child in a car be transported in an approved child restraint system?
options: 1.25 metres
1.35 metres
1.45 metres
1.50 metres
rule-kinderzitje.explanation: Under article 35.1.1, children under 1.35 metres in height must be transported in an approved child restraint system suited to their weight/height.

rule-gsm.question: Are you as a driver allowed to hold your mobile phone in your hand while driving?
options: Yes, if you hold it on speaker.
No, holding or manipulating a mobile device in your hand is prohibited while driving.
Yes, but only when you are stationary at a red light.
Yes, if you drive slower than 30 km/h.
rule-gsm.explanation: Article 8.4 prohibits holding, using, or manipulating any mobile electronic device with a screen in your hand while driving, unless the vehicle is properly parked.

rule-voorrang-rechts.question: Who has priority at an intersection where priority is not regulated by signs, lights, or an official?
options: The driver coming from the right.
The driver coming from the left.
The driver on the widest road.
The driver driving fastest.
rule-voorrang-rechts.explanation: Article 12.3.1 establishes the general rule of priority to the right at uncontrolled intersections.

rule-voorrang-rechts-gestopt.question: Do you lose your priority from the right if you stop briefly at the intersection before pulling away?
options: Yes, if you stop you always lose your priority.
No, stopping briefly does not cause you to lose your priority to the right (according to consistent Belgian case law).
Only if you stop for longer than 3 seconds.
Only if you step off your bicycle or turn off your engine.
rule-voorrang-rechts-gestopt.explanation: According to the Belgian Court of Cassation, a driver with priority from the right retains priority even after stopping briefly to check cross traffic.

rule-rotonde.question: Who has priority on a roundabout indicated by sign D5 and B1 with yield teeth?
options: The driver already on the roundabout.
The driver wishing to enter the roundabout (priority from the right).
Traffic entering from the left.
The largest vehicle.
rule-rotonde.explanation: Sign B1 and road markings at the entrance mean circulating drivers on the roundabout have priority (art. 12.3.1).

rule-prioritair.question: What must you do when a priority vehicle with flashing blue lights and siren approaches?
options: Maintain your speed and drive in the middle of the road.
Immediately clear the way, move to the side, and stop if necessary.
Speed up to stay ahead of the vehicle.
Only make way on motorways.
rule-prioritair.explanation: Under article 38, all drivers must immediately clear the way and give priority to a priority vehicle using both its blue beacons and siren.

rule-fietser-inhalen.question: What lateral clearance must you maintain at least when overtaking a cyclist inside a built-up area?
options: 0.5 metre
1.0 metre
1.5 metres
2.0 metres
rule-fietser-inhalen.explanation: Under article 40ter, drivers must maintain at least 1.0 metre lateral clearance inside built-up areas (and at least 1.5 metres outside).

rule-zebra.question: What must you do when a pedestrian is crossing or clearly about to step onto a pedestrian crossing?
options: Accelerate to pass before the pedestrian steps onto the crossing.
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian.
Give priority to the pedestrian and stop if necessary.
Pedestrians must always wait for cars.
rule-zebra.explanation: Under article 40.4.1, drivers must yield priority and stop if necessary for pedestrians on or about to step onto a pedestrian crossing.

rule-fietser-aan-hand.question: How is a person walking with a bicycle in hand treated under traffic law?
options: As a cyclist.
As a pedestrian.
As a moped rider.
As an extraordinary road user.
rule-fietser-aan-hand.explanation: Under article 2.16, a person pushing a bicycle or two-wheeled moped by hand is treated as a pedestrian.

rule-verzekering.question: What is legally mandatory for any motor vehicle driven on the public road in Belgium?
options: Only a valid roadworthiness certificate.
A valid third-party liability motor insurance policy (BA auto).
A comprehensive fully comprehensive insurance policy.
A breakdown assistance policy.
rule-verzekering.explanation: Under Belgian law, third-party liability insurance (burgerlijke aansprakelijkheid) is legally compulsory for every motor vehicle on the public road.

rule-reddingsstrook.question: What must you do when traffic slows to a queue on a motorway with at least two lanes in your direction?
options: Drive onto the hard shoulder.
Form an emergency rescue lane between the leftmost lane and the adjacent lane.
Stop on your lane and switch on hazard lights.
Overtake on the right.
rule-reddingsstrook.explanation: Under article 2.70, drivers in queuing traffic must proactively form an emergency rescue corridor between the leftmost lane and the adjacent lane.

rule-mistlichten.question: When are rear fog lights mandatory on a car in Belgium?
options: In fog or snowfall reducing visibility to less than 100 metres, and in heavy rain.
In all rain showers.
Between sunset and sunrise in all conditions.
Only in fog reducing visibility to less than 200 metres.
rule-mistlichten.explanation: Under article 30.1.2, rear fog lights must be used in fog or snow reducing visibility to under 100 m, and during heavy rain.

rule-rijbewijs-begeleider.question: From what age can you obtain a provisional driving licence (Category B) with a supervising guide in Belgium?
options: 16 years old
17 years old
18 years old
19 years old
rule-rijbewijs-begeleider.explanation: Under the Belgian learner driver system, candidates can obtain a provisional licence with guide (VRB 36M) from 17 years of age.

rule-begeleider-ervaring.question: How many years must a supervising guide hold a Belgian or European driving licence category B at least?
options: 3 years
5 years
8 years
10 years
rule-begeleider-ervaring.explanation: A supervising guide must have held a Category B driving licence for at least 8 years and must not have had a driving ban within the last 3 years.

rule-overweg.question: What must you do when approaching a railway level crossing with flashing red lights or moving barriers?
options: Drive through quickly if no train is visible.
Stop before the stop line or barrier and wait until the lights stop flashing and the barriers are fully open.
Slalom through if only one half-barrier is down.
Sound your horn and proceed.
rule-overweg.explanation: Article 20.1 obliges drivers to stop immediately when red lights flash or barriers move at a railway crossing.

rule-zone30.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a designated Zone 30?
options: 20 km/h
30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
rule-zone30.explanation: In a Zone 30 (sign F4a), the speed limit is 30 km/h for all road users across the entire zone (art. 65.5).

rule-estep-helm-2026.question: From what design speed is a safety helmet mandatory on an electric scooter or moped in Belgium?
options: From 15 km/h
From 25 km/h (Class B moped / Speed Pedelec)
Helmets are never mandatory for e-scooters.
From 10 km/h
rule-estep-helm-2026.explanation: A helmet is mandatory for vehicles exceeding 25 km/h (such as speed pedelecs and class B mopeds) under article 36.

rule-vierwieler-helm-2024.question: Must the driver of a quad or light four-wheeler wear a helmet if the vehicle is not fitted with seat belts?
options: Yes, wearing an approved crash helmet is mandatory without seat belts.
No, a helmet is only required for two-wheelers.
Only on motorways.
Only under the age of 18.
rule-vierwieler-helm-2024.explanation: Under article 36, drivers and passengers of quads without seat belts must wear an approved protective helmet.

rule-middenrijbaan-2022.question: Where should you drive on a road designed with a central roadway and two lateral cycle/pedestrian verges (sign F117)?
options: On the central lane, moving to the lateral verge only when passing oncoming traffic without endangering cyclists.
Always on the lateral verge.
Wherever you prefer.
Cars are banned on these roads.
rule-middenrijbaan-2022.explanation: On a central roadway (middenrijbaan, art. 75.3), drivers use the central lane and temporarily cross into the lateral verge only when passing oncoming vehicles safely.

rule-estep-leeftijd-2022.question: From what minimum age is riding a motorised e-scooter permitted on the public road in Belgium (except in residential/pedestrian zones)?
options: 12 years
14 years
16 years
18 years
rule-estep-leeftijd-2022.explanation: Since 2022, the minimum age for riding a motorised personal mobility device on public roads is 16 years (art. 8.2bis).

rule-estep-passagier-2022.question: Are two people allowed to ride on a single electric scooter on the public road?
options: Yes, if both hold the handlebar.
No, carrying passengers on an e-scooter is strictly prohibited.
Yes, if the combined weight is under 100 kg.
Yes, in pedestrian zones only.
rule-estep-passagier-2022.explanation: Article 8.2bis strictly prohibits transporting passengers on motorised personal mobility devices.

rule-speed-pedelec-d9-2022.question: May a speed pedelec rider use a mandatory cycle and pedestrian path (sign D9)?
options: Yes, but only if an additional plate with the bicycle/moped symbol or 'P' indicates it.
Yes, always at any speed.
No, speed pedelecs are never allowed on D9 paths.
Only during off-peak hours.
rule-speed-pedelec-d9-2022.explanation: Under article 9.1.2, speed pedelecs may only use D9 paths if explicitly authorized by an additional plate (symbol P).

rule-velomobiel-2022.question: What extra visibility requirement applies to a velomobile (recumbent cycle) on the public road?
options: A safety flag and reflective strips when lower than 1 metre.
A siren.
A roof light.
No special rules apply.
rule-velomobiel-2022.explanation: Recumbent bicycles and velomobiles lower than 1 metre must be equipped with a reflective safety flag or markings for visibility (art. 82.1).

rule-fietsstraat-f111-2021.question: How far do the specific rules of a cycle street (sign F111) apply?
options: Until the next intersection or until end sign F113.
Always for exactly 500 metres.
Only until the first traffic light.
Throughout the whole municipality.
rule-fietsstraat-f111-2021.explanation: The cycle street regime applies up to the end sign F113 or the next intersection unless renewed (art. 22novies).

rule-brussel-stad30-2021.question: What has been the standard speed limit in built-up areas in the Brussels-Capital Region since 2021?
options: 20 km/h
30 km/h (City 30)
50 km/h
70 km/h
rule-brussel-stad30-2021.explanation: Since 1 January 2021, 30 km/h is the general default speed limit in the Brussels-Capital Region (City 30).

rec-b19.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Smalle doorgang waarbij je priority moet verlenen aan tegenliggers
Smalle doorgang waarbij tegenliggers priority moeten verlenen aan jou
End of a priority road
Mandatory rechtdoor rijden
rec-b19.explanation: Bord B19 legt op dat je bij een smalle doorgang priority moet verlenen aan drivers die uit de tegenovergestelde richting komen (art. 67.3).

rec-b3.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Advance warning of sign B1 (give way) at the indicated distance
Advance warning of sign B5 (stoppen en give way) at the indicated distance
give way aan alle drivers at the intersection
intersection waar de priority to the right geldt
rec-b3.explanation: Bord B3 kondigt bord B1 (give way) aan op de bij benadering indicated afstand (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b7.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Advance warning of sign B1 (give way) at the indicated distance
Advance warning of sign B5 (stoppen en give way) at the indicated distance
Mandatory stoppen bij het bord en give way
Gevaarlijke drempel at the indicated distance
rec-b7.explanation: Bord B7 kondigt bord B5 (stoppen en give way) aan op de bij benadering indicated afstand (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b11.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Beginning of a priority road
Advance notice of het einde van de priority road op afstand
End of the priority road
intersection met priority to the right
rec-b11.explanation: Bord B11 duidt het einde van een priority road aan (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b13.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: End of the priority road vanaf dit bord
Beginning of a priority road at the indicated distance
priority op het eerstvolgende intersection
Advance notice of het einde van de priority road at the indicated distance
rec-b13.explanation: Bord B13 kondigt het einde van de priority road (bord B11) aan op de bij benadering indicated afstand (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b15.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: priority op het eerstvolgende intersection
Beginning of a priority road
intersection waar priority to the right geldt
Smalle doorgang met priority op tegenliggers
rec-b15.explanation: Bord B15 indicates that drivers priority hebben op het eerstvolgende intersection (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b21.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Smalle doorgang waarbij je priority moet verlenen aan tegenliggers
Smalle doorgang met priority ten opzichte van tegenliggers
one-way traffic in de indicated rijrichting
dead end
rec-b21.explanation: Bord B21 duidt een smalle doorgang aan waarbij je priority hebt ten opzichte van tegemoetkomende drivers (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b22.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory cycle path met afslag naar rechts
cyclists en speedpedelecs mogen bij rood licht rechtdoor rijden mits priority
cyclists en speedpedelecs mogen bij rood licht rechtsaf slaan mits priority te verlenen
Prohibition for cyclists om rechtsaf te slaan bij rood licht
rec-b22.explanation: Bord B22 laat cyclists en drivers of speedpedelecs toe om bij rood of oranjegeel licht rechtsaf te slaan, mits zij give way (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-b23.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: cyclists en speedpedelecs mogen bij rood licht rechtsaf slaan mits priority
Mandatory cycle path rechtdoor
Reserved lane voor cyclists en speedpedelecs
cyclists en speedpedelecs mogen bij rood licht rechtdoor rijden mits priority te verlenen
rec-b23.explanation: Bord B23 laat cyclists en drivers of speedpedelecs toe om bij rood of oranjegeel licht rechtdoor te rijden, mits zij give way (art. 67 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c31a.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory links afslaan op het next intersection
Prohibited to turn left at the next intersection
one-way traffic naar links
dead end aan de linkerkant
rec-c31a.explanation: Bord C31a prohibits aan het eerstvolgende intersection links af te slaan in de richting van de pijl (art. 68.3).

rec-c33.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Prohibition against rechts af te slaan
Mandatory keren op de roadway
Prohibition against te keren (U-bocht maken)
Scherpe bocht naar links
rec-c33.explanation: Bord C33 prohibits drivers om te keren (een U-bocht te maken) tot aan het volgende intersection (art. 68.3).

rec-c39.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Overtaking prohibited for all motor vehicles
No entry for lorries
Mandatory lane voor lorries
Overtaking prohibited for lorries with a MAM exceeding 3.5 tonnes
rec-c39.explanation: Bord C39 prohibits lorries met een maximale toegelaten massa van meer dan 3,5 ton om een gespan of motor vehicle met meer dan twee wielen in te halen (art. 68.3).

rec-c5.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for drivers of motor vehicles with more than two wheels and motorcycles with sidecar
No entry for alle motor vehicles, inclusief tweewielige motorcycles zonder zijspan
Mandatory lane reserved for carpoolers en taxi's
No entry for drivers of goods vehicles
rec-c5.explanation: Bord C5 prohibits de Access voor drivers of motor vehicles with more than two wheels and motorcycles with sidecar (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975). Tweewielige motorcycles zonder zijspan mogen hier wel rijden.

rec-c6.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for alle vierwielige agricultural vehicles en tractoren
No entry for drivers of vierwielige motor vehicles geconstrueerd voor onverhard terrein (quads)
Mandatory route for quads en terreinvoertuigen
No entry for mopeds met vier wielen
rec-c6.explanation: Bord C6 prohibits de Access voor drivers of vierwielige motor vehicles met een open carrosserie, stuur als op een motorcycle en zadel, ontworpen voor onverhard terrein, zoals quads (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c7.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for mopeds en speedpedelecs
Mandatory parkeerstrook voor tweewielige motor vehicles
No entry for drivers of motorcycles
Overtaking prohibited for alle drivers of motorcycles
rec-c7.explanation: Bord C7 prohibits de Access voor drivers of motorcycles (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c9.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for rijwielen en speedpedelecs
Mandatory cycle path voor class B mopeds
No entry for alle gemotoriseerde tweewielers boven 50 cc
No entry for riders of mopeds
rec-c9.explanation: Bord C9 prohibits de Access voor riders of mopeds (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c11.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for drivers of rijwielen
Mandatory cycle path voor cyclists en speedpedelecs
No entry for pedestrians en voortbewegingstoestellen
End of the verplichte cycle path
rec-c11.explanation: Bord C11 prohibits de Access voor drivers of rijwielen (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c13.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for ruiters en bereden dieren
No entry for drivers of gespannen
Mandatory route for paarden en huifkarren
No entry for agricultural vehicles
rec-c13.explanation: Bord C13 prohibits de Access voor drivers of gespannen (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c15.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for drivers of gespannen
Mandatory weg voor ruiters (ruiterpad)
No entry for ruiters
Warning of overstekend vee of paarden
rec-c15.explanation: Bord C15 prohibits de Access voor ruiters (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c17.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for pedestrians met kinderwagens
Mandatory laad- en loszone voor handkarren
No entry for kruiwagens op het trottoir
No entry for drivers of handkarren
rec-c17.explanation: Bord C17 prohibits de Access voor drivers of handkarren (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c19.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for pedestrians
Mandatory weg voor pedestrians (voetpad)
crossing voor pedestrians
End of the voetgangersgebied
rec-c19.explanation: Bord C19 prohibits de Access voor pedestrians (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c21.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for vehicles met een maximale toegelaten massa (MAM (maximum authorised mass)) boven de indicated massa
No entry for drivers of vehicles waarvan de massa in beladen toestand hoger is dan de indicated massa
Mandatory maximale aslast per as voor lorries
Recommended maximumgewicht voor lorries en bussen
rec-c21.explanation: Bord C21 prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles waarvan de werkelijke massa in beladen toestand (MBTA) hoger is dan de indicated massa (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c22.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for geregelde diensten voor gemeenschappelijk openbaar vervoer
Parkeerverbod voor autobussen en touringcars
No entry for drivers of autocars
Reserved lane voor autobussen en autocars
rec-c22.explanation: Bord C22 prohibits de Access voor drivers of autocars (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c23.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for alle motor vehicles met aanhangwagen
Overtaking prohibited for vrachtauto's van meer dan 3,5 ton
Mandatory lane voor goederenvervoer
No entry for drivers of motor vehicles en slepen ontworpen en gebouwd voor het vervoer van goederen
rec-c23.explanation: Bord C23 prohibits de Access voor drivers of motor vehicles en slepen ontworpen en gebouwd voor goederenvervoer (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c24a.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for drivers of vehicles die gevaarlijke goederen vervoeren
Mandatory rijrichting voor vehicles die gevaarlijke goederen vervoeren
No entry for vehicles met ontvlambare of ontplofbare stoffen
Prohibition against gevaarlijke goederen te laden of lossen binnen de built-up area
rec-c24a.explanation: Bord C24a prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles die gevaarlijke goederen vervoeren (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c24b.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for alle vehicles met een LPG- of aardgasinstallatie
No entry for drivers of vehicles die gevaarlijke ontvlambare of ontplofbare stoffen vervoeren
No entry for vehicles die waterverontreinigende stoffen vervoeren
Prohibition op open vuur en roken nabij tankstations
rec-c24b.explanation: Bord C24b prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles die gevaarlijke ontvlambare of ontplofbare stoffen vervoeren (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c24c.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for vehicles die ontvlambare gassen vervoeren
Prohibition against vloeistoffen of afval te lozen in oppervlaktewater
No entry for drivers of vehicles die gevaarlijke verontreinigende stoffen vervoeren
Warning of a waterwingebied met verhoogd overstromingsrisico
rec-c24c.explanation: Bord C24c prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles die gevaarlijke verontreinigende stoffen vervoeren (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c25.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for gelede bussen en lorries met aanhangwagen
Recommended minimale afstand tot voorliggers voor lange vehicles
Mandatory volgafstand van minstens de indicated afstand in meters
No entry for drivers of vehicles of slepen waarvan de lengte, lading inbegrepen, groter is dan de indicated
rec-c25.explanation: Bord C25 prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles of slepen waarvan de lengte, lading inbegrepen, groter is dan aangeduid op het bord (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c27.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: No entry for drivers of vehicles waarvan de breedte, lading inbegrepen, groter is dan de indicated
Warning of a road narrowing langs beide zijden van de weg
Recommended minimale passeerbreedte voor agricultural vehicles
Prohibition against op een lane smaller dan de indicated maat in te halen
rec-c27.explanation: Bord C27 prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles waarvan de breedte, lading inbegrepen, groter is dan de indicated maat (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c29.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Warning of a viaduct of tunnel met beperkte doorgangshoogte
No entry for drivers of vehicles waarvan de hoogte, lading inbegrepen, groter is dan de indicated
Recommended doorrijhoogte voor touringcars en dubbeldekkers
Mandatory minimumhoogte voor bedrijfsvoertuigen onder het kunstwerk
rec-c29.explanation: Bord C29 prohibits de Access voor drivers of vehicles waarvan de hoogte, lading inbegrepen, groter is dan de indicated hoogte (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c31b.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory rijrichting rechtsaf op het eerstvolgend intersection
Eenrichtingsweg met verboden Access vanaf de rechterzijde
Prohibition aan het next intersection af te slaan in de richting door de pijl aangegeven (rechts)
dead-end street aan de eerstvolgende afslag rechts
rec-c31b.explanation: Bord C31b prohibits op het eerstvolgende intersection af te slaan in de richting aangeduid door de pijl, hier rechtsaf (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c37.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Beginning of a zone met Overtaking prohibited for all motor vehicles
End of the Overtaking prohibited uitsluitend voor lorries boven 3,5 ton
Prohibition against vehicles met meer dan twee wielen langs rechts in te halen
End of the Prohibition een gespan of een vehicle met meer dan twee wielen links in te halen
rec-c37.explanation: Bord C37 duidt het einde aan van het Overtaking prohibited dat was opgelegd door bord C35 (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c41.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: End of the Prohibition voor goederenvoertuigen with a MAM exceeding 3.5 tonnes om links in te halen
End of the algemeen Overtaking prohibited for personenauto's en motorcycles
Beginning of a Overtaking prohibited for lorries bij regenweer
Mandatory lane voor vrachtauto's with a MAM over 3.5 tonnes
rec-c41.explanation: Bord C41 duidt het einde aan van het Overtaking prohibited for drivers of vehicles gebruikt voor goederenvervoer with a MAM exceeding 3.5 tonnes (einde bord C39, art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c43.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Recommended speed up to het next intersection
Prohibition te rijden met een grotere snelheid dan deze die is aangeduid tot het next intersection
Mandatory minimumsnelheid op dit wegvak
Beginning of a zonale speed limit die enkel eindigt bij een zone-eindebord
rec-c43.explanation: Bord C43 prohibits te rijden met een grotere snelheid dan aangeduid, vanaf het bord tot het next intersection, tenzij anders aangegeven (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c45.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: End of alle plaatselijke verbodsbepalingen voor vehicles in beweging
End of the adviessnelheid op het betrokken wegvak
End of the speed limit opgelegd door het traffic sign C43
End of the minimale snelheid op deze public weg
rec-c45.explanation: Bord C45 duidt het einde aan van de speed limit die eerder werd opgelegd door bord C43 (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c46.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: End of alle parkeer- en stilstandverboden op deze weg
End of the motorway of expressway
End of the priority road bij het eerstvolgende intersection
End of alle plaatselijke verbodsbepalingen opgelegd aan de vehicles in beweging
rec-c46.explanation: Bord C46 duidt het einde aan van alle plaatselijke verbodsbepalingen die eerder werden opgelegd aan vehicles in beweging, zoals snelheidsbeperkingen en inhaalverboden (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-c47.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

Mandatory weegbrug en aslastcontrole voor lorries
Grensovergang waar uitsluitend lorries moeten stoppen
Tolpost: Prohibition voorbij te rijden zonder te stoppen
rec-c47.explanation: Bord C47 (Tolpost of Taks) legt een Prohibition op om voorbij te rijden zonder te stoppen (art. 68 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-d9.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory cycle path waar pedestrians verboden zijn
pedestrian zone waar fietsen niet is toegestaan
crossing voor cyclists en pedestrians
Deel van de public weg reserved for pedestrians, cyclists en bromfietsers klasse A
rec-d9.explanation: Bord D9 duidt een deel van de public weg aan dat reserved is voor het verkeer van pedestrians, cyclists en tweewielige class A mopeds (art. 69.3).

rec-d10.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: cycle path uitsluitend bestemd voor racefietsen
Deel van de public weg reserved for pedestrians en cyclists (zonder mopeds)
Beginning of a residential area / living street
Mandatory voetpad waar cyclists niet mogen rijden
rec-d10.explanation: Bord D10 duidt een pad aan reserved for pedestrians en cyclists; in tegenstelling tot bord D9 mogen class A mopeds hier niet rijden (art. 69.3).

rec-d1b.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory rijrichting: links
Mandatory rijrichting: rechtdoor rijden
Obligation to de hindernis langs links voorbij te rijden
Prohibition against links af te slaan
rec-d1b.explanation: Dit gebodsbord (D1) obliges je de rijrichting van de pijl te volgen, hier links (art. 69.3 van de Highway Code).

rec-d1c.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Obligation to de hindernis langs rechts voorbij te rijden
Obligation to de hindernis langs links voorbij te rijden
Mandatory rijrichting linksaf at the intersection
one-way traffic naar links
rec-d1c.explanation: Bord D1c legt de verplichting op om de hindernis langs de door de pijl indicated zijde voorbij te rijden, hier links (art. 69 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-d1d.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Obligation to de hindernis langs links voorbij te rijden
Mandatory rijrichting rechtsaf at the intersection
Obligation to de hindernis langs rechts voorbij te rijden
dangerous bend to the right
rec-d1d.explanation: Bord D1d legt de verplichting op om de hindernis langs de door de pijl indicated zijde voorbij te rijden, hier rechts (art. 69 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-d1e.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory rijrichting: rechtdoor rijden
Obligation to de hindernis langs links voorbij te rijden
dead-end street aan de linkerzijde
Mandatory rijrichting: links
rec-d1e.explanation: Dit gebodsbord (D1, alternatieve uitvoering) obliges je de rijrichting van de pijl te volgen, hier links (art. 69.3 van de Highway Code).

rec-d3.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Obligation to één van de door de pijlen indicated richtingen te volgen
Mandatory rijrichting uitsluitend rechtdoor
intersection waar priority to the right geldt
Prohibition against rechtdoor of rechtsaf te rijden
rec-d3.explanation: Bord D3 obliges drivers om één van de door de pijlen indicated richtingen te volgen, hier rechtdoor of rechtsaf (art. 69 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-d4.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Toegangsverbod voor vehicles die gevaarlijke goederen vervoeren
Mandatory rijrichting voor vehicles die gevaarlijke goederen vervoeren
Recommended route for lorries with a MAM exceeding 3.5 tonnes
Mandatory rijrichting voor alle bedrijfsvoertuigen
rec-d4.explanation: Bord D4 legt een Mandatory direction of travel op voor vehicles die gevaarlijke goederen vervoeren (art. 69 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-d11.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Mandatory cycle path waar pedestrians mogen wandelen
pedestrian zone waar cyclists stapvoets mogen rijden
Mandatory weg voor pedestrians (voetpad)
crossing voor pedestrians
rec-d11.explanation: Bord D11 legt een verplichte weg voor pedestrians op; dit pad is uitsluitend reserved for pedestrians (art. 69 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-d13.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Toegangsverbod voor ruiters en gespannen vehicles
Warning of overstekend groot wild of vee
Deel van de public weg reserved for agricultural vehicles
Mandatory weg voor ruiters (ruiterpad)
rec-d13.explanation: Bord D13 legt een verplichte weg voor ruiters op; dit pad is uitsluitend reserved for bereden dieren (art. 69 Royal Decree 1 December 1975).

rec-e3.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Enkel parkeerverbod
Reserved parkeerplaats
Stilstaan en no parking
End of a parkeerzone
rec-e3.explanation: Bord E3 betekent dat zowel stilstaan als no parking is aan de zijde van de public weg waar het bord staat (art. 70.2.1).

rec-e5.question: What does this traffic sign mean?

Parkeerverbod van de 16e tot het einde van de maand
Stilstaan en no parking gedurende de eerste twee weken
Reserved parking space for één vehicle
rec-e5.explanation: Bord E5 legt een parkeerverbod op langs de kant van de weg waar het staat, van de 1e tot de 15e van de maand (art. 70.2.1).

rec-e7.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Parkeerverbod van de 1e tot de 15e van de maand
Parkeerverbod van de 16e tot het einde van de maand
Prohibited: te parkeren op feestdagen en in het weekend
Beurtelings parkeren met een maximale parkeertijd van 2 uur
rec-e7.explanation: Bord E7 legt een parkeerverbod op langs de kant van de weg waar het staat, van de 16e tot het einde van de maand (art. 70.2.1).

rec-e9a.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Parkeerplaats voor ziekenwagens
Parkeerverbod voor mindervaliden
crossing voor wheelchair users
Parkeerplaats reserved for persons with disabilities
rec-e9a.explanation: Bord E9a met rolstoelsymbool indicates that het parkeren uitsluitend reserved is voor vehicles gebruikt door persons with disabilities met een speciale parkeerkaart (art. 70.2.1).

rec-e9b.question: What does this traffic sign mean?
options: Parkeren uitsluitend voor vrachtauto's en autobussen

Parkeren uitsluitend voor motorcycles, personenauto's, auto's voor dubbelgebruik en minibussen

rule-estep-trottoir-2022.question: Are you allowed to ride a motorised e-scooter on the pavement (footway)?
options: Yes, provided you ride at walking pace.
No, motorized e-scooters are equated with bicycles and must not use the pavement (except when walked).
Yes, outside built-up areas.
Yes, if there are no pedestrians.
rule-estep-trottoir-2022.explanation: Motorised personal mobility devices are equated with bicycles and are banned from pavements, regardless of speed (art. 7bis).

rule-estep-snelheid-2022.question: What is the maximum design speed permitted for a motorised personal mobility device (e-scooter) in Belgium?
options: 18 km/h
20 km/h
25 km/h
30 km/h
rule-estep-snelheid-2022.explanation: Under article 2.15.2, motorised personal mobility devices must have a maximum design speed of 25 km/h.

rule-estep-parkeren-2022.question: Where are you allowed to leave a shared electric scooter after your ride?
options: Anywhere on the pavement as long as it does not obstruct traffic completely.
In designated drop-off zones (dropzones) or properly parked without hindering pedestrians.
In the middle of the cycle path.
On a zebra crossing.
rule-estep-parkeren-2022.explanation: E-scooters must be parked in marked drop-off zones or on pavements without obstructing pedestrian passage (art. 7bis).

rule-gsm-houder-2022.question: Under what condition is a driver permitted to use a mobile phone for navigation while driving?
options: Only if the device is securely fastened in a dedicated holder attached to the vehicle.
Held in your lap.
Held loosely in one hand.
Only when driving under 50 km/h.
rule-gsm-houder-2022.explanation: Article 8.4 requires any screen device used while driving to be secured in a dedicated mounting holder attached to the vehicle.

rule-speed-pedelec-rijbewijs-2022.question: Which driving licence must you hold at least to ride a speed pedelec (up to 45 km/h) in Belgium?
options: No driving licence required.
At least a Category AM (moped) driving licence or a full Category B licence.
A motorcycle Category A licence.
A special cyclist licence.
rule-speed-pedelec-rijbewijs-2022.explanation: A speed pedelec is classified as a moped class P, requiring at least a Category AM or B driving licence.

rule-speed-pedelec-snelheid-2022.question: Up to what maximum speed may pedal assistance operate on a speed pedelec?
options: 25 km/h
35 km/h
45 km/h
50 km/h
rule-speed-pedelec-snelheid-2022.explanation: Under European and Belgian regulations, a speed pedelec provides pedal assistance up to a maximum speed of 45 km/h.

rule-velomobiel-hoogte-2022.question: Where on a velomobile must mandatory reflective markings be placed?
options: On both lateral sides and the rear.
Only on the pedals.
Only on the front.
No reflectors required.
rule-velomobiel-hoogte-2022.explanation: Velomobiles and low recumbents must feature retro-reflective markings on the sides and rear to remain visible to other drivers (art. 82.1).

rule-reddingsstrook-vorming-2022.question: How must drivers on a three-lane road form an emergency rescue lane in traffic congestion?
options: Left lane moves to the left; the middle and right lanes move to the right.
All lanes move to the left.
All lanes move onto the hard shoulder.
Middle lane stays stationary.
rule-reddingsstrook-vorming-2022.explanation: On roads with three or more lanes, the leftmost lane moves left, while all other lanes move right, leaving a rescue corridor next to the leftmost lane (art. 2.70).

rule-ritsen-locatie.question: Where should drivers merge when zipper merging (zippering) in slowing traffic before a lane reduction?
options: As early as possible when you see the first warning sign.
Right at the point where the lane actually terminates (at the bottleneck).
100 metres before the end of the lane.
Whenever someone lets you in.
rule-ritsen-locatie.explanation: Article 12bis obliges drivers to drive up to the lane obstruction and merge alternately right at the bottleneck (zipper merging).

rule-ritsen-voorrang.question: How does priority work during mandatory zipper merging at the point of lane reduction?
options: Drivers in the continuing lane must alternately give right of way to one merging driver.
The continuing lane always has absolute priority.
The faster driver always goes first.
The vehicle on the right always has priority.
rule-ritsen-voorrang.explanation: Under article 12bis, drivers in the continuing lane must grant priority alternately to one driver from each ending lane.

rule-fietsstraat-inhalen.question: Is a car allowed to overtake a cyclist in a cycle street (fietsstraat)?
options: Yes, with 1 metre clearance.
No, motor vehicles are strictly forbidden from overtaking cyclists in a cycle street.
Yes, if the cyclist signals to pass.
Only if driving faster than 25 km/h.
rule-fietsstraat-inhalen.explanation: Under article 22novies, motor vehicles are never allowed to overtake cyclists in a cycle street.

rule-fietsstraat-snelheid.question: What is the absolute maximum speed limit for all traffic in a cycle street?
options: 20 km/h
30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
rule-fietsstraat-snelheid.explanation: In a cycle street (fietsstraat), the maximum speed limit is 30 km/h for all vehicles (art. 22novies).

rule-fietser-b22.question: What does authorisation sign B22 allow cyclists and riders of personal mobility devices to do?
options: Turn right through a red or amber traffic light, yielding priority to other road users.
Ride straight through on red.
Ignore all STOP signs.
Ride on the pavement.
rule-fietser-b22.explanation: Sign B22 permits cyclists to turn right cautiously at red or amber lights, yielding priority to crossing pedestrians and other traffic (art. 67.3).

rule-fietser-b23.question: What does authorisation sign B23 allow cyclists to do at a traffic light?
options: Continue straight ahead through a red light, yielding priority to crossing traffic.
Turn left on red.
U-turn on red.
Ride without lights.
rule-fietser-b23.explanation: Sign B23 allows cyclists to continue straight ahead through red or amber lights, yielding priority to all other road users (art. 67.3).

rule-voorrang-aardeweg.question: Does a driver coming from the right from an unpaved dirt track (aardeweg) onto a paved road have priority?
options: Yes, priority to the right always applies.
No, a driver emerging from an unpaved dirt track must yield priority to drivers on the paved road.
Only if they are driving a tractor.
Only in built-up areas.
rule-voorrang-aardeweg.explanation: Under article 12.3.1, a driver emerging from an unpaved road or dirt track onto a paved road must yield priority to all traffic on the paved road.

rule-voorrang-uitrit.question: Who has priority when a driver emerges from a private garage, driveway, or car park onto the public road?
options: The emerging driver has priority from the right.
Traffic already on the public road has priority; emerging is a manoeuvre requiring you to yield to all users.
Whoever arrives first.
The vehicle with the highest speed.
rule-voorrang-uitrit.explanation: Emerging from a private property or car park is a manoeuvre (art. 12.4); the driver must yield priority to all other road users.

rule-voorrang-afslaan-tegenligger.question: You are turning left at an uncontrolled intersection. Must you yield priority to oncoming traffic continuing straight ahead?
options: No, priority from the right applies to your turn.
Yes, a driver turning left must yield priority to oncoming traffic continuing straight or turning right.
Only to heavy goods vehicles.
Only if there is a STOP sign.
rule-voorrang-afslaan-tegenligger.explanation: Under article 19.3.1, a driver turning left must yield priority to oncoming traffic on the same roadway.

rule-voorrang-tram-algemeen.question: Does general priority from the right apply against a tram?
options: Yes, a tram must always give way to vehicles from its right.
No, trams have priority over other road users at uncontrolled intersections, regardless of whether they approach from the left or right.
Only outside built-up areas.
Only on single-track lines.
rule-voorrang-tram-algemeen.explanation: Under article 12.3.2, trams have absolute priority over other road users at equal intersections, except against priority signs or traffic lights.

rule-voorrang-tram-voetganger.question: Must a tram stop for a pedestrian crossing on a zebra crossing?
options: Yes, pedestrians always have absolute priority over all vehicles including trams.
No, pedestrians must yield priority to trams, even on a zebra crossing.
Only if the pedestrian is accompanied by a guide dog.
Only in pedestrian zones.
rule-voorrang-tram-voetganger.explanation: Under article 40.4.1, the obligation to give way to pedestrians on a zebra crossing applies to drivers of road vehicles, but pedestrians must give way to trams.

rule-bus-bebouwde-kom.question: What must you do inside a built-up area when a public transport bus indicates its intention to leave a bus stop?
options: Accelerate to pass before the bus pulls out.
Slow down and stop if necessary to let the bus pull out safely.
Sound your horn to assert your priority.
Buses never have priority when leaving a stop.
rule-bus-bebouwde-kom.explanation: Under article 39, drivers in built-up areas must slow down and allow public buses to pull out from marked stops when their indicator is on.

rule-bus-buiten-bebouwde-kom.question: Must you stop outside a built-up area for a public bus signaling to leave a bus stop?
options: Yes, the rule is the same everywhere.
No, the obligation to give way to departing buses applies only within built-up areas.
Only on provincial roads.
Only if the speed limit is 70 km/h.
rule-bus-buiten-bebouwde-kom.explanation: The obligation to give way to departing scheduled buses under article 39 applies strictly inside built-up areas, not outside.

rule-manoeuvre-achteruitrijden.question: Who has priority when you are reversing out of a parking bay into the street?
options: You have priority because you are already moving.
All other road users have priority over a reversing vehicle performing a manoeuvre.
Pedestrians must wait, but cars have priority.
Priority from the right applies.
rule-manoeuvre-achteruitrijden.explanation: Reversing is a manoeuvre under article 12.4; the driver performing it must give way to all other road users.

rule-manoeuvre-rijstrookwissel.question: What is the rule when you want to change lanes on a multi-lane road?
options: Changing lanes is a manoeuvre; you must yield priority to traffic already in the target lane.
You automatically have priority once you signal.
Traffic behind you must brake.
Priority from the right applies to lane changes.
rule-manoeuvre-rijstrookwissel.explanation: Changing lanes is a manoeuvre (art. 12.4); you must indicate, check mirrors/blind spots, and yield priority to traffic in the target lane.

rule-oversteekplaats-fietser.question: Does a cyclist crossing at a designated cyclist crossing (marked by two parallel broken white squares) have priority over approaching cars?
options: Yes, cars must always stop for cyclists on a cycle crossing.
No, cyclists entering a cycle crossing must yield priority to approaching traffic on the roadway.
Only if the cyclist is under 18.
Only in a built-up area.
rule-oversteekplaats-fietser.explanation: Under article 40ter, a cyclist entering a bicycle crossing must yield priority to approaching traffic, unlike pedestrians on zebra crossings.

rule-fietser-op-zebrapad.question: Does a cyclist who rides across a zebra crossing without dismounting enjoy pedestrian priority?
options: Yes, anyone on a zebra crossing has priority.
No, a riding cyclist is not a pedestrian and does not have priority on a zebra crossing.
Yes, provided they ride slower than 10 km/h.
Only on school zebra crossings.
rule-fietser-op-zebrapad.explanation: Under article 40.4.1, zebra crossing priority applies strictly to pedestrians (and persons pushing a bicycle on foot), not to riding cyclists.

rule-parkeren-zebrapad-afstand.question: At what minimum distance before a pedestrian crossing is stopping or parking on the roadway prohibited?
options: At least 3 metres
At least 5 metres
At least 10 metres
At least 15 metres
rule-parkeren-zebrapad-afstand.explanation: Under article 24.4°, it is prohibited to stop or park a vehicle on the roadway within 5 metres before a pedestrian crossing.

rule-parkeren-bushalte-afstand.question: Within what distance on either side of a bus stop sign is parking prohibited on the roadway (if not marked otherwise)?
options: 5 metres
10 metres
15 metres
20 metres
rule-parkeren-bushalte-afstand.explanation: Under article 25.1.2°, parking is prohibited within 15 metres on either side of a bus or tram stop sign on the roadway.

rule-stilstaan-vs-parkeren.question: What is the strict legal difference between stopping (stilstaan) and parking (parkeren) under the Highway Code?
options: Stopping is immobilising the vehicle only for the time needed to board/alight passengers or load/unload goods; parking is any longer stay.
Stopping is for up to 15 minutes; parking is longer than 15 minutes.
Stopping is with engine running; parking is with engine turned off.
There is no legal difference.
rule-stilstaan-vs-parkeren.explanation: Under article 2.22/2.23, stopping is strictly limited to the duration required to embark/disembark persons or load/unload goods; anything else is parking.

rule-parkeren-kruispunt-afstand.question: Within what distance from the edge of the intersecting roadway at an intersection is parking prohibited?
options: Less than 3 metres
Less than 5 metres
Less than 10 metres
Less than 15 metres
rule-parkeren-kruispunt-afstand.explanation: Under article 25.1.1°, parking is prohibited on the roadway within 5 metres of the corner/intersection.

rule-parkeren-brandkraan.question: At what distance from a fire hydrant or underground hydrant cover is parking prohibited?
options: Within 1 metre
Within 5 metres
Directly above or opposite an underground fire hydrant cover/marker.
Only in industrial estates.
rule-parkeren-brandkraan.explanation: Under article 25.1.8°, parking is prohibited on covers providing access to underground fire hydrants or public utilities.

rule-verlichting-tunnels.question: Which lights are legally mandatory when driving through a road tunnel during daytime?
options: Dipped-beam headlights (dimlichten).
Daytime running lights are sufficient.
Hazard warning lights.
Fog lights.
rule-verlichting-tunnels.explanation: Under article 30.1, dipped headlights (low beam) must be used in all road tunnels indicated by sign F89, regardless of ambient daylight.

rule-verlichting-duisternis.question: From what reduced visibility during daylight hours (due to fog, snow, or rain) are dipped headlights mandatory?
options: When visibility is less than 500 metres.
When visibility is reduced to less than 200 metres.
When visibility is less than 50 metres.
Only at complete nightfall.
rule-verlichting-duisternis.explanation: Under article 30.1, dipped headlights are mandatory between nightfall and dawn, and by day whenever visibility is reduced to under 200 metres.

rule-grootlicht-tegenligger.question: What must you do with your high-beam headlights (grootlichten) when oncoming traffic approaches?
options: Switch immediately from high-beam to dipped-beam headlights.
Maintain high beam if driving fast.
Flash your lights twice.
Switch off all lights.
rule-grootlicht-tegenligger.explanation: Under article 30.2, high-beam headlights must be dipped immediately when oncoming vehicles approach or when following closely behind another vehicle.

rule-inhalen-kruispunt.question: Are you permitted to overtake another car on the left at an intersection where priority to the right applies?
options: No, overtaking a multi-track vehicle on the left is prohibited at intersections where priority to the right applies.
Yes, if you sound your horn.
Yes, if the road has two lanes.
Only outside built-up areas.
rule-inhalen-kruispunt.explanation: Under article 16.4.1°, overtaking on the left is prohibited at intersections where drivers must yield priority to the right.

rule-inhalen-oversteekplaats.question: Are you permitted to overtake a vehicle that is slowing down or stopping before a pedestrian crossing?
options: No, overtaking a vehicle that is slowing down or stopped before an unsignalled pedestrian crossing is strictly prohibited.
Yes, if you drive at walking pace.
Yes, if you indicate.
Only if no pedestrians are visible.
rule-inhalen-oversteekplaats.explanation: Under article 16.4.2°, overtaking a vehicle approaching or stopped before an unsignalled pedestrian crossing is strictly prohibited.

rule-snelheid-woonerf.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a residential area (woonerf) or living street (erf)?
options: 10 km/h
20 km/h
30 km/h
50 km/h
rule-snelheid-woonerf.explanation: In a woonerf or erf (sign F12a), the speed limit is 20 km/h for all vehicular traffic (art. 22bis).

rule-woonerf-voetganger.question: What special rule applies to pedestrians and playing children in a residential area (woonerf)?
options: They may use the entire width of the street and play, and drivers must not impede them.
They must stay on the pavement.
They only have priority between 9:00 and 18:00.
Children must be accompanied by adults.
rule-woonerf-voetganger.explanation: In a residential area (woonerf, art. 22bis), pedestrians may use the full street width and games are permitted; drivers must not endanger or obstruct them.

rule-slepen-snelheid.question: What is the maximum speed when one car is towing another broken-down vehicle with a tow rope or bar?
options: 25 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
70 km/h
rule-slepen-snelheid.explanation: Under article 49.1, the maximum speed when towing a broken-down vehicle on public roads is 25 km/h.

rule-alcohol-alarmfase.question: What immediate measure does the police impose for an alcohol breath test result in the 'Alert' range (0.5 to 0.8 promille)?
options: An immediate 3-hour temporary driving ban.
An immediate 6-hour temporary driving ban.
Immediate confiscation of the vehicle.
No immediate measure.
rule-alcohol-alarmfase.explanation: An 'Alert' result (0.22 to 0.35 mg/l UAL) results in an immediate 3-hour driving ban imposed by the police (art. 60 §3).

rule-alcohol-positief-3uur.question: How long is the temporary driving ban imposed by police for a 'Positive' breath test result (0.8 promille or higher)?
options: 3 hours
6 hours
12 hours
24 hours
rule-alcohol-positief-3uur.explanation: A 'Positive' result (≥ 0.35 mg/l UAL or ≥ 0.8 promille) results in an immediate temporary driving ban of at least 6 hours (art. 60 §3).

rule-autosnelweg-omkeren.question: Are you permitted to reverse or make a U-turn on a motorway if you missed your exit?
options: No, reversing, U-turning, and driving against traffic on a motorway are strictly prohibited.
Yes, on the hard shoulder with hazard lights on.
Yes, at emergency crossover points in the central reservation.
Only between midnight and 5 a.m.
rule-autosnelweg-omkeren.explanation: Under article 21.4, making U-turns, reversing, or driving across the central reservation on motorways is strictly forbidden.

rule-autosnelweg-pechstrook.question: When are you permitted to use the hard shoulder (pechstrook) on a motorway?
options: Only in the event of an unavoidable vehicle breakdown, emergency, or when dynamic signs open it as a running lane.
To make a brief phone call.
To bypass heavy traffic congestion.
To take a rest break.
rule-autosnelweg-pechstrook.explanation: Under article 21.4, the hard shoulder may only be used in case of breakdown or absolute emergency, or when instructed by police/dynamic signs.

rule-autosnelweg-inhalen-rechts.question: When are you permitted to overtake another car on the right on a motorway?
options: Never.
In dense queuing traffic (fileverkeer) moving in parallel lanes, or when following direction arrows over your lane.
Whenever the left lane is driving under the speed limit.
Only during nighttime.
rule-autosnelweg-inhalen-rechts.explanation: Under article 16.2, passing on the right is permitted in traffic congestion moving in parallel lanes (fileverkeer) or when following designated lane destination arrows.

rule-rotonde-pinker.question: When are you obliged to use your right-hand indicator on a roundabout in Belgium?
options: When entering the roundabout.
When you are about to leave the roundabout (before your chosen exit).
Continuously while driving around.
Never.
rule-rotonde-pinker.explanation: Under article 19.2, drivers must indicate to the right immediately before taking their exit when leaving a roundabout, but not when entering.

rule-rotonde-voorsorteren.question: Which lane should you preferably take on a multi-lane roundabout if you intend to take the first exit (turning right)?
options: The outermost (right) lane.
The innermost (left) lane.
The lane does not matter.
The middle of both lanes.
rule-rotonde-voorsorteren.explanation: Drivers taking the first exit should enter and remain in the outer right-hand lane of the roundabout (art. 9.1).

rule-schoolbus-gevaarslichten.question: What must you do when a stationary school bus or bus transporting children has its four hazard warning lights flashing?
options: Slow down considerably and stop if necessary to allow children to cross safely.
Maintain normal speed.
Overtake as quickly as possible.
Sound your horn.
rule-schoolbus-gevaarslichten.explanation: Under article 39bis, drivers approaching a school bus with hazard lights flashing must slow down significantly and stop if necessary.

rule-fietser-naast-elkaar.question: Are two cyclists permitted to ride side by side on the roadway outside a built-up area?
options: Yes, provided they move into single file when an oncoming vehicle approaches or when passing from behind is not otherwise possible.
No, outside built-up areas they must always ride in single file.
Yes, without any restrictions.
Only on cycle paths.
rule-fietser-naast-elkaar.explanation: Under article 43.1, cyclists may ride two abreast outside built-up areas, but must move into single file when approached from the front or rear when passing cannot occur safely.

sit-01-b5-stop.question: You are cycling to school and arrive at this intersection with a STOP sign. Do you have to stop here?
options: No, as a cyclist I only need to slow down slightly.
Yes, I must come to a complete stop and give priority to traffic from the left and right.
No, a STOP sign applies only to motor vehicles.
sit-01-b5-stop.explanation: A STOP sign (B5) obliges every driver (including cyclists) to stop completely at the stop line and give priority to drivers on the crossing road.

sit-02-b17-voorrang-rechts.question: You arrive at this intersection with traffic sign B17. What must you do?
options: I must stop and give priority to drivers from the left and right.
I may simply proceed because sign B17 gives me priority.
I slow down and give priority to drivers coming from the right.
sit-02-b17-voorrang-rechts.explanation: Traffic sign B17 indicates that you are approaching an intersection where the general rule of priority to the right applies (art. 12.3.1).

sit-03-b1-haaientanden.question: You arrive by bicycle at this intersection with sign B1 and yield teeth (give-way markings). What must you do?
options: I slow down and give priority to drivers on the crossing road (from the left and right).
I must always stop with a foot on the ground, even if no traffic is approaching.
I may proceed freely, as yield teeth only apply to motorists.
sit-03-b1-haaientanden.explanation: Traffic sign B1 (inverted triangle) and give-way road markings oblige you to give priority to drivers on the crossing road. Stopping is only required if necessary.

sit-04-b22-rechtsaf-rood.question: The traffic light is red, but sign B22 (yellow bicycle with arrow) is mounted on the post. Are you allowed to turn right?
options: Yes, but only if there is no pedestrian crossing at all.
Yes, you may turn right on red provided you yield priority to other road users.
No, at a red light you must always wait until it turns green.
sit-04-b22-rechtsaf-rood.explanation: Traffic sign B22 allows cyclists to turn right carefully through a red or amber light, provided they yield priority to other road users.

sit-05-f49-zebrapad-fietser.question: A pedestrian is crossing at the zebra crossing and a cyclist is approaching. Who must yield priority?
options: The pedestrian must stop for the cyclist.
The cyclist only has to yield if the pedestrian is already past the halfway point.
The cyclist must yield priority to the crossing pedestrian.
sit-05-f49-zebrapad-fietser.explanation: Drivers (including cyclists) must give priority to pedestrians who are on a crossing or about to step onto it (art. 40.4.1).

sit-06-b19-smalle-doorgang.question: You approach this narrow passage with traffic sign B19. Who may proceed first?
options: Oncoming traffic: sign B19 obliges you to give priority to approaching oncoming drivers.
You may proceed first because oncoming traffic has a red arrow on their sign.
Whoever is driving fastest may go through first.
sit-06-b19-smalle-doorgang.explanation: Sign B19 (round with red arrow for your direction and black arrow for oncoming traffic) obliges you to give priority to oncoming traffic in the narrow passage.

sit-07-kruispunt-drie-fietsers.question: Three cyclists arrive simultaneously at this uncontrolled intersection of equal roads. Who may proceed first?
options: Cyclist A, because nobody is coming from their right.
Cyclist C, because they are cycling straight ahead.
All three cyclists must step off their bicycles.
sit-07-kruispunt-drie-fietsers.explanation: At an intersection without priority signs, priority to the right applies: cyclist A has no traffic on their right, so cyclist A may proceed first.

sit-08-licht-boven-bord.question: The traffic light is green, but there is also a STOP sign on the post. What must you do?
options: You follow the green traffic light and may proceed carefully; the light takes precedence over the sign.
You must stop at the STOP sign regardless of the light.
You must first wait for the traffic light to turn red.
sit-08-licht-boven-bord.explanation: Traffic signals (lights) take precedence over traffic signs (art. 6.2). When the traffic light is functioning, it overrides the STOP sign.

sit-09-fietszone-f111.question: You are driving in this cycle street (cycle zone, sign F111). Which rule applies here to motorists?
options: Motorists may overtake cyclists at a maximum speed of 50 km/h.
Motorists are never allowed to overtake cyclists and the maximum speed is 30 km/h.
Motorists have priority over cyclists.
sit-09-fietszone-f111.explanation: In a cycle street (sign F111), motor vehicles must not overtake cyclists under any circumstances, and the speed limit is 30 km/h (art. 22novies).

sit-10-politieagent-halt.question: The police officer stands across the intersection with arms extended horizontally. What does this order mean?
options: Stop for traffic approaching from the front and from behind the officer.
Stop for traffic approaching from the sides.
All traffic must turn right.
sit-10-politieagent-halt.explanation: Arms outstretched horizontally means 'Stop' for road users approaching from directions facing the officer's front or back (art. 4.2.1).

sit-11-plaats-geen-fietspad.question: There is no cycle path on this road, only a pavement (footway). Where must a cyclist (aged 10 or older) ride?
options: On the pavement, provided you ring your bell.
On the right side of the roadway.
Cyclists are not allowed on this road.
sit-11-plaats-geen-fietspad.explanation: If there is no cycle path, cyclists aged 10 and older must ride on the roadway, keeping to the right (art. 9.1.2).

sit-12-step-trottoir.question: You are riding a non-motorised scooter on a public road. Where must you ride?
options: If you move at walking pace, you follow the rules for pedestrians; if faster than walking pace, you follow the rules for cyclists.
Always on the roadway between cars.
You are only allowed to ride on private property.
sit-12-step-trottoir.explanation: Users of non-motorised mobility devices who travel no faster than walking pace follow pedestrian rules; travelling faster than walking pace, they follow cyclist rules (art. 7bis).

sit-13-bebouwde-kom-naast-elkaar.question: Two cyclists are riding side by side in a built-up area and a car approaches behind them. What must the cyclists do?
options: They may remain riding side by side, provided the road is wide enough to be passed safely.
They must immediately dismount.
Cyclists are never allowed to ride side by side in a built-up area.
sit-13-bebouwde-kom-naast-elkaar.explanation: In a built-up area, two cyclists may ride side by side, but they must ride in single file when an oncoming vehicle approaches or when passing is not otherwise possible (art. 43.1).

sit-14-fietspad-d7-enkelrichting.question: Are you allowed to cycle in the opposite direction on this cycle path indicated by sign D7?
options: Yes, a cycle path is always two-way.
No, sign D7 indicates a one-way cycle path on the right side of the road in your direction of travel.
Yes, but only if you have your bicycle lights on.
sit-14-fietspad-d7-enkelrichting.explanation: A cycle path indicated by sign D7 on the right side of the road must be used in the direction of travel, unless an additional plate explicitly indicates two-way cycling (art. 9.1.2).

sit-15-kind-voetpad.question: Up to what age are children allowed to ride a bicycle on the pavement (footway)?
options: Up to 10 years of age (with wheel diameter up to 50 cm, provided they do not endanger pedestrians).
Up to 16 years of age.
Children are never allowed to cycle on the pavement.
sit-15-kind-voetpad.explanation: Children under 10 years of age may ride on the pavement on bicycles with wheels not exceeding 50 cm in diameter, provided they do not endanger pedestrians (art. 9.1.2).

sit-16-voetganger-links-rijbaan.question: There is no pavement, verge, or cycle path present. On which side of the roadway must pedestrians walk?
options: On the left side in their direction of travel (facing oncoming traffic).
On the right side in their direction of travel.
Right in the middle of the roadway.
sit-16-voetganger-links-rijbaan.explanation: When pedestrians must walk on the roadway, they must keep to the left side in their direction of travel so they can see oncoming traffic (art. 42.2).

sit-17-b9-voorrangsweg.question: You are driving on this road with traffic sign B9 (yellow diamond). Which priority rule applies here?
options: You are on a priority road and have priority at intersections until sign B11.
You must give priority to everyone coming from the right.
This sign only indicates a dead end.
sit-17-b9-voorrangsweg.explanation: Sign B9 indicates that you are on a priority road and have priority over crossing traffic at subsequent intersections until an end-of-priority sign B11.

sit-18-b21-voorrang-tegenliggers.question: You approach this narrow passage with traffic sign B21 (blue square with white and red arrows). Who may proceed first?
options: You have priority over oncoming traffic in this narrow section.
Oncoming traffic has priority over you.
Both drivers must stop and negotiate.
sit-18-b21-voorrang-tegenliggers.explanation: Sign B21 (blue square with white arrow in your direction) grants you priority over oncoming traffic in the narrow passage (art. 67.3).

sit-19-f19-beperkt-eenrichting.question: You are cycling towards this street with sign F19 and additional plate M2 (bicycle with arrows). What does this mean?
options: This is a one-way street for cars, but cyclists are allowed to ride in both directions (limited one-way traffic).
Cyclists are not allowed to enter this street.
Cyclists must walk on the pavement.
sit-19-f19-beperkt-eenrichting.explanation: Sign F19 with additional plate M2/M3 indicates limited one-way traffic (SUL): motor vehicles may only travel in one direction, while cyclists may ride in both directions.

sit-20-f4a-zone-30.question: You drive past traffic sign F4a (zone 30). What speed limit applies from here?
options: Maximum 30 km/h in the entire zone, until the zone end sign F4b.
30 km/h only up to the next intersection.
30 km/h only during school opening hours.
sit-20-f4a-zone-30.explanation: A zonal sign (F4a) applies to all streets within the designated area until the end-of-zone sign F4b (art. 65.5).

sit-21-rotonde-voorrang.question: You approach this roundabout marked with sign D5 and B1 with yield teeth. Who has priority?
options: Drivers already on the roundabout have priority over entering traffic.
Drivers entering have priority from the right.
The largest vehicle always has priority.
sit-21-rotonde-voorrang.explanation: On a roundabout marked with sign D5 and sign B1 with yield teeth, drivers already circulating on the roundabout have priority (art. 12.3.1).

sit-22-overweg-slagbomen.question: The red lights are flashing and the level crossing barriers are coming down. What must you do?
options: Stop before the stop line or barrier and wait until the lights stop flashing and the barriers are fully raised.
Quickly accelerate to cross before the barriers close completely.
Slalom around the barriers if no train is visible.
sit-22-overweg-slagbomen.explanation: When red lights flash or barriers move at a level crossing, you must stop immediately and never attempt to cross (art. 20.1).

sit-23-voorsorteren-pijlen.question: You are in the lane with an arrow pointing left. Are you allowed to go straight ahead at the intersection?
options: No, you are obliged to follow the direction indicated by the lane arrow.
Yes, lane arrows are merely recommendations.
Yes, provided you signal with your indicator.
sit-23-voorsorteren-pijlen.explanation: Direction arrows painted on lanes are mandatory: drivers in a marked lane must follow the indicated direction (art. 77.1).

sit-24-fietssuggestiestrook.question: You are driving along this reddish-ochre cycle advisory lane (without sign D7 or a broken white line). Are you allowed to drive on it?
options: Yes, a cycle advisory lane is part of the roadway; cars may drive on it, but must not endanger cyclists.
No, this is a mandatory cycle path where cars are strictly forbidden.
Only on Sundays and public holidays.
sit-24-fietssuggestiestrook.explanation: A cycle advisory lane is not an official cycle path: it is part of the roadway meant to increase cyclist visibility; motorists may drive on it, but cannot park on it (art. 2.15.2).

sit-25-erf-woonerf-f12a.question: You enter a street marked with traffic sign F12a (residential zone / living street). Which rule applies to pedestrians and speed?
options: Maximum speed 20 km/h; pedestrians may use the full width of the street and play, and drivers must not impede them.
Maximum speed 30 km/h; pedestrians must stay on the pavement.
Maximum speed 50 km/h; normal traffic rules apply.
sit-25-erf-woonerf-f12a.explanation: In a residential zone (sign F12a), the speed limit is 20 km/h, pedestrians may use the entire street width and play, and drivers must not endanger or obstruct them (art. 22bis).

sit-26-prioritair-voertuig.question: An ambulance is approaching behind you with flashing blue lights and its siren sounding. What must you do?
options: Immediately clear the path, move to the side, and stop if necessary to let the vehicle pass.
Maintain your speed and stay in the middle of your lane.
Accelerate to stay ahead of the ambulance.
sit-26-prioritair-voertuig.explanation: As soon as a priority vehicle uses both its blue flashing lights and special sound warning, all road users must immediately clear the way and give priority (art. 38).

sit-27-doorlopende-witte-streep.question: You are driving behind a slow tractor on a road with a solid white line. Are you allowed to overtake the tractor by crossing the solid line?
options: No, you must never cross or straddle a continuous white line, even to overtake slow vehicles.
Yes, overtaking tractors is an exception to the solid white line rule.
Yes, if you flash your headlights first.
sit-27-doorlopende-witte-streep.explanation: A continuous white line must never be crossed or straddled, with no exception for slow agricultural vehicles (art. 72.2).

sit-28-parkeren-trottoir-verbod.question: Are you allowed to park your car with two wheels on the pavement as shown, if there is no sign E9b?
options: No, parking on the pavement is prohibited unless explicitly authorised by sign E9b or ground markings.
Yes, as long as half the pavement remains free for pedestrians.
Yes, provided it is outside a built-up area.
sit-28-parkeren-trottoir-verbod.explanation: Vehicles must be parked on the roadway or verge; parking on the pavement is strictly prohibited unless authorised by sign E9b or specific markings (art. 24.1).

sit-29-busstrook-f17.question: You are driving a private passenger car. Are you allowed to drive on this special bus lane (sign F17 and 'BUS' marking)?
options: No, unless you need to change direction at the immediate next intersection.
Yes, anyone may use a bus lane outside peak hours.
Yes, provided you drive faster than 50 km/h.
sit-29-busstrook-f17.explanation: A bus lane (sign F17) is reserved for public transport buses; other drivers may only enter it in the immediate vicinity of an intersection to change direction (art. 72.5).

sit-30-blindengeleidehond-oversteken.question: A person with a white cane or a guide dog wants to cross the road. What must you do as an approaching driver?
options: Stop in all circumstances and allow them to cross safely, even if there is no pedestrian crossing.
Sound your horn to alert them that you are passing.
Maintain your speed because pedestrians without a crossing have no priority.
sit-30-blindengeleidehond-oversteken.explanation: Drivers must in all circumstances stop and grant passage to blind persons carrying a white cane or accompanied by a guide dog (art. 40.2).

sit-31-rechtsaf-fietser-voorrang.question: You want to turn right by car at this intersection while a cyclist is continuing straight ahead on the cycle path. Who has priority?
options: The cyclist continuing straight ahead has priority over the turning car.
The car has priority because it is larger.
Priority to the right applies, so the car has priority.
sit-31-rechtsaf-fietser-voorrang.explanation: A driver changing direction must yield priority to road users continuing straight on the same road, including cyclists on an adjacent cycle path (art. 19.3.2).

sit-32-knipperlicht-beweegbare-brug.question: You approach this movable bridge where two red lights are flashing alternately. What does this signal mean?
options: Obligatory stop: the bridge is opening or open, and passage is prohibited.
You may drive through slowly if you see no boats.
The lights are defective; proceed with caution.
sit-32-knipperlicht-beweegbare-brug.explanation: Alternately flashing red lights at a movable bridge mean an absolute prohibition on proceeding (art. 64.1).

sit-33-geel-knipperlicht-kruispunt.question: The traffic lights at this intersection are flashing amber and there are no priority signs. Which priority rule applies?
options: The general rule of priority to the right applies.
Traffic on the widest street automatically has priority.
All vehicles must come to a complete stop.
sit-33-geel-knipperlicht-kruispunt.explanation: When traffic lights flash amber and there are no priority signs, the lights are deactivated and standard priority to the right applies (art. 12.3.1).

sit-34-fietsopstelvak-f107.question: Where must motorists stop at a red traffic light with an advanced stop box for cyclists (ASL, sign F107) on the roadway?
options: Before the first stop line, keeping the designated bike box clear for cyclists.
Inside the bike box, as close to the traffic light as possible.
Next to the cyclists in the bike box.
sit-34-fietsopstelvak-f107.explanation: Motorists must stop before the first stop line, leaving the advanced stop box (sign F107) completely free for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds (art. 77.7).

sit-35-schoolstraat-c3.question: What does sign C3 with the 'Schoolstraat' plate at the start of this street mean during the indicated hours?
options: The street is temporarily closed to all motor vehicle traffic at school start and finish times.
Cars may enter, but must drive at a maximum speed of 10 km/h.
Only parents of pupils are allowed to drive in.
sit-35-schoolstraat-c3.explanation: A school street is closed to motor vehicles during designated school hours to allow children and pedestrians safe access (art. 2.68).

sit-36-spitsstrook-matrixbord.question: On the overhead gantry above the hard shoulder / dynamic lane, a green arrow pointing down is illuminated. Are you allowed to drive on this lane?
options: Yes, a green arrow indicates that the hard shoulder is currently open as a dynamic running lane.
No, the hard shoulder is always strictly reserved for breakdowns.
Yes, but only for lorries.
sit-36-spitsstrook-matrixbord.explanation: A green arrow illuminated on an overhead lane control sign indicates that the dynamic hard shoulder is opened to running traffic (art. 65.4).

sit-37-tram-halte-uitstappen.question: A tram stops on the roadway at a stop without a raised platform, and passengers are getting off. What must you do as a following motorist?
options: Stop behind the tram and wait until all passengers have safely reached the pavement.
Carefully overtake the tram on the left.
Sound your horn and drive through at walking pace.
sit-37-tram-halte-uitstappen.explanation: When a tram stops without a platform, following drivers must stop to allow passengers to board and alight safely to and from the pavement (art. 40.5).

sit-38-bevoegd-persoon-arm-omhoog.question: A police officer stands at an intersection with one arm raised vertically. What does this order mean?
options: Attention / Stop for all road users from all directions, except those already inside the intersection.
Traffic from the left may turn.
All vehicles must accelerate to clear the intersection.
sit-38-bevoegd-persoon-arm-omhoog.explanation: An arm raised vertically by an authorized official means attention/stop for all traffic from all directions, clearing the intersection (art. 4.2.2).

sit-39-afstand-inhalen-fietser.question: What is the minimum lateral distance a car must maintain when overtaking a cyclist outside a built-up area?
options: At least 1.5 metres.
At least 1.0 metre.
At least 0.5 metre.
sit-39-afstand-inhalen-fietser.explanation: When overtaking a cyclist outside a built-up area, drivers must leave a lateral clearance of at least 1.5 metres (inside built-up areas: 1.0 metre) (art. 40ter).

sit-40-reddingsstrook-file.question: Traffic congestion forms on a motorway with two lanes. How must drivers form an emergency rescue lane?
options: Vehicles in the left lane move as far left as possible; vehicles in the right lane move as far right as possible, leaving the space between them clear.
All vehicles drive onto the hard shoulder.
Drivers stop in the middle of their lanes and wait.
sit-40-reddingsstrook-file.explanation: In traffic queues, drivers in the leftmost lane move to the left, and drivers in the right lane move to the right, forming an emergency rescue corridor between them without using the hard shoulder (art. 2.70).
